title: Skiing in Türkiye, Winter 2026–27: Erciyes, Uludağ, Palandöken, Kartalkaya or Sarıkamış?
excerpt: A decision framework for choosing a Turkish ski resort this winter: access, sightseeing pairings, resort style and lift pass rules, plus what to confirm before you book.

body.text: Türkiye has more than one serious ski mountain, and the five names travellers ask about most are Erciyes, Uludağ, Palandöken, Kartalkaya and Sarıkamış. They are not interchangeable. Each sits in a different region, pairs with a different city or sightseeing trip, and suits a different kind of skier. This guide gives you a way to choose for the December 2026 to March 2027 season, and a checklist of what to confirm with the resort operator before you pay for flights and hotels. It deliberately contains no snow forecasts and no ski pass prices: both change, and the operator is the only reliable place to read them.
First, a word on opening dates

Turkish ski areas open when snow and lift operators allow, not on a fixed calendar date. When we checked on 11 November 2026, the only 2026–27 date we found on a resort information site was on [uludaginfo.com](https://uludaginfo.com/en), the Uludağ information portal, whose events list showed a “2026–2027 Season Opening” entry on 18 December; the same page said 2026–27 season passes were on sale online. The portal calls itself an official information portal for the resort, but its footer names a software company (DYB Yazılım Danışmanlık A.Ş.) rather than the lift operator, so treat that as a planned date, not a guarantee, and confirm it with the operator before booking. We did not find a confirmed 2026–27 opening date from an official source for Erciyes, Palandöken, Kartalkaya or Sarıkamış. If your trip falls in the first half of December, book refundable hotel nights or keep the dates flexible until the resort announces that lifts are running.
The five resorts at a glance

items: Erciyes (Kayseri, Central Anatolia): GoTürkiye describes the mountain as an extinct volcano with dramatic angles and plenty of snow. The Culture and Tourism Ministry’s resort page places it about 25 km south of Kayseri and describes skiing on the eastern and northern slopes between roughly 2,200 m and 3,100 m below the 3,916 m summit; that page appears dated, so check the current slope map. Best pairing: Cappadocia.

Uludağ (above Bursa, Marmara region): GoTürkiye calls it Türkiye’s oldest and most popular ski resort, close to both Bursa and Istanbul, with a cable car serving the hotel area and slopes. The uludaginfo.com portal describes four separate ski zones. Best pairing: Bursa, or a short add-on to an Istanbul stay.
Palandöken (Erzurum, Eastern Anatolia): GoTürkiye presents it as a preferred destination for skilled skiers, with steep slopes, long runs and light powder. Best pairing: the city of Erzurum.

Kartalkaya (Köroğlu Mountains, Bolu): GoTürkiye notes it is close to both Istanbul and Ankara, popular with snowboarders, with expert-only off-piste terrain and options for cross-country skiing; Yedigöller National Park is described as a day trip. Best pairing: a mountain-hotel break between the two big cities.
Sarıkamış (near Kars, Eastern Anatolia): GoTürkiye places it 55 km from Kars and describes nine slopes for all levels. Best pairing: Kars and a winter train journey.

body.text: Step 1: Decide what the trip is really for

Start with one honest question: is this a ski holiday with some sightseeing, or a Türkiye trip with a few days on snow? If skiing is the main event, prioritise terrain and snow reliability, and accept a longer journey east. If sightseeing matters as much, choose the mountain that sits next to the place you already want to visit, so that a bad-weather day on the slopes becomes a good day in town rather than a wasted one.

items: Ski first, sightseeing second: Palandöken or Sarıkamış for experienced skiers who want a dedicated mountain trip; Erciyes if you want high-altitude skiing with Cappadocia nearby.
Culture first, skiing second: Erciyes plus Cappadocia, or Uludağ plus Bursa.
Short break from Istanbul or Ankara: Uludağ or Kartalkaya.
Mixed group of beginners and stronger skiers: look for a resort with clearly separated beginner terrain and ski school options, and read its current slope map before booking.

body.text: Step 2: Match the mountain to your sightseeing

Erciyes and Cappadocia are the most natural pairing. GoTürkiye’s Erciyes page lists Kayseri Castle and the Cappadocia towns of Göreme, Ürgüp, Avanos and Uçhisar among things to see, although it gives no travel times. Build in buffer days, because winter wind and snow affect both ski lifts and hot-air balloon flights. Our [Cappadocia hot-air balloon guide](/blog/cappadocia-hot-air-balloon-guide) explains how weather cancellations work, and our [private Türkiye itinerary guide](/blog/private-turkiye-itinerary-cappadocia-guide) shows how to fit Cappadocia into a longer route.

Uludağ pairs with Bursa, the city below the mountain, so a day of skiing and a day in town fit easily into one short break. The uludaginfo.com portal describes several ways up, including the cable car, private car, ferry and airport transfer, with routes listed from Istanbul, Mudanya and Sabiha Gökçen. Check the cable car’s live status on the day, as wind can affect it.

Palandöken pairs with Erzurum, and Sarıkamış with Kars. GoTürkiye presents both as part of a winter trip along the Eastern Express railway. If you are planning the Touristic Eastern Express, read our [Ankara–Kars sleeper train planning guide](/blog/touristic-eastern-express-ankara-kars-planning): its sightseeing stops differ by direction, so check whether your train calls where you need it before you plan a ski day around it.

Access is where trips succeed or fail. For Erciyes, the Culture and Tourism Ministry’s resort page says the mountain is about 30 minutes by road from Kayseri city centre and about 40 minutes from Kayseri airport. That page appears to be older (its lift description is out of date), so confirm current transfer times with your hotel. For the other four resorts we did not find official, current transfer times, so we have not invented them. Ask each hotel or transfer company three things: which airport or station they collect from, how long the transfer takes in winter conditions, and what happens if the road or cable car is closed.
Step 4: Read the lift pass rules before you buy

Lift pass rules vary by operator, and many travellers only read them after something goes wrong. The Uludağ [skipass rules](https://www.uludaginfo.com/en/skipass-rules) published on the uludaginfo.com portal (last updated 18 May 2026 when we checked) are a good example of what to look for; confirm them at the ticket office when you buy:

items: Passes are personal, except points-based entry tickets; a shared personal pass can be blocked.
No refunds for bad weather, facilities not opening or blocked passes, and none if lifts close during the day for weather or breakdowns.
Passes are valid only in the season they were bought; 3-hour tickets work only on the day of purchase from the first scan, and flexible tickets cover a set number of days within 30 days.
A lost or damaged card is replaced only with the serial number and the receipt; the replacement fee shown was 100 TL, which can change.
Helmets are mandatory while skiing, and pedestrian tickets are sold separately from ski passes.
Tickets bought from unauthorised sellers may be blocked or confiscated.

body.text: Do not assume the same rules apply at Erciyes, Palandöken, Kartalkaya or Sarıkamış. Find the equivalent page on each operator’s website, or ask at the ticket office, before buying a multi-day pass.

items: Has the resort operator announced that lifts are open, or only a planned opening date?
Which lifts and slopes are running on your dates? Check the live lift and slope status on the operator’s site.
What are the current pass prices, and are they shown for the 2026–27 season?
Are passes refundable or transferable, and what happens if lifts close for wind?
Is a helmet required, and can you rent one on site?
How long is the transfer from your arrival airport or station in winter, and is it shared or private?
Do your hotel’s cancellation terms protect you if the season opens late?
Does your travel insurance cover winter sports, including off-piste if you plan to ski it?

body.text: If you are still deciding when to travel, our [month-by-month guide](/blog/best-time-to-visit-turkiye-month-by-month) and our [Türkiye in winter guide](/blog/turkey-in-winter-premium-travel-guide) help you weigh a ski week against city and coastal options in the same season.

seo.intent: Choose between Türkiye’s main ski resorts for winter 2026–27 and know what to confirm (opening, access, lift pass rules) before booking.
seo.uniqueValue: Compares five Turkish ski resorts by trip purpose, sightseeing pairing, access and lift pass rules; reports only operator- or GoTürkiye-sourced facts, flags that 2026–27 opening dates are snow-dependent, and gives a before-booking checklist instead of invented prices or snow claims.

quality.reviewNotes: Draft by a writer subagent; independent reviewer re-opened all five sources: Uludağ 18 Dec opening framed as planned per uludaginfo.com, which is described as a portal not shown to be the lift operator; refund wording narrowed to the cases the page names; KTB Erciyes altitudes/distances flagged as from an older page. No opening dates, snow conditions or prices invented for other resorts. Translation review of DE, zh-CN, KO, ES done, links verified. Editorial attestation, not native-speaker certification.
